chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yunus ibn Ammar, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Suleyman! You are upon a Religion; whoever conceals it, Allah honors him, and whoever broadcasts it, Allah humiliates him.'

key_terms.أَذَاعَهُ: He broadcasted it / made it known publicly

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of concealing versus broadcasting one's religion or state?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi encapsulates the core Shia doctrine of *al-Din al-Mu'assas* (the established religion) and its relationship with *Taqiyya* (dissimulation), emphasizing that the preservation of faith often requires strategic concealment from hostile powers. Historically, this reflects the socio-political reality of the Imams' era, where public declaration could lead to persecution, thus linking spiritual honor to the wisdom of keeping one's true beliefs guarded. It serves as a theological justification for why Shia identity and practices were not always immediately visible or publicly proclaimed in early Islamic history.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Yunus Bin Ammar, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Suleyman! You all are upon such a Religion that the one who conceals it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Honours him, and the one who broadcasts it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Humiliates him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Yunus ibn ‘Ammar from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) once said, ‘O Sulayman, you follow the religion of one for whose silent abstinence Allah grants him honor, but due to his loud publicity, Allah causes his humiliation. ’”
